title: DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() is inconsistent
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.7.2.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.3.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M2 - Apple M2 (8 threads) - 8.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I'm trying to estimate the Pixels Per Inch (PPI) of the main display. It may also be called physical DPI. The following should hold:
`PPI ≈ DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() / DisplayServer.screen_get_scale()`

Theres a few issues that prevented me:
On macOS, DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() is wrong.
On Android, DisplayServer.screen_get_scale() is wrong.

Assuming that DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() is meant to return logical DPI, it is subject to UI scale so that my formula should hold true. macOS seems to already apply the scale and return physical DPI. On my MacBook, I expect 448 dpi because UI scale is 2.0, but it returns 224 dpi. On my Android phone the physical DPI is 507, but the function returns 345 because I have my "Screen Zoom" set to minimum. Increasing "Screen Zoom" increases the logical DPI.

DisplayServer.screen_get_scale() is meant to return UI scale (akin to Window.content_scale_factor) which the user adjusts in their display settings. It does not depend on physical DPI. It tells you how many physical pixels make up a logical pixel, or at least how big logical pixels are compared to a baseline. On macOS it returns 2.0 for Retina displays, which makes sense to me. On Android it returns a normalised version of DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi(), which does not help convert to physical pixels at all.

There are inconsistencies in how DPI is calculated for non-square pixels:
On macOS, DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() is calculated using the diagonal length.
On Linux, DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() is calculated using the average (arithmetic mean).

Ideally, Godot will expose the physical size of the display in future so I can calculate the exact PPI. But that can be handled elsewhere. This issue is about getting DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() and DisplayServer.screen_get_scale() to behave consistently.

### Steps to reproduce

Inspect the values of DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi() and DisplayServer.screen_get_scale() on various platforms
